renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: novel_support
  title: Novel precursors by support
  description: |-
    Each point is a novel miRNA precursor merged across samples: the number of samples that report it and its best miRDeep2 score, sized by its total reads and coloured by whether star-arm reads were seen. It answers which candidates are best supported.
    How to read: candidates in the upper right are detected in many samples with a high score. A star-arm read pair is the signature of Dicer processing, so a candidate with star support is stronger than one without. Open the table to read the sequences of the labelled candidates.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median best miRDeep2 score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of miRDeep2. The README sets a score cut-off of 0 only for which novel candidates its overview table lists.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rajewsky-lab/mirdeep2/master/README.md and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21911355/
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    x_title: Samples reporting the precursor
    y_title: Best miRDeep2 score
    legend_pos: bottom
    top_n_labels: 6
  roles:
    x: samples_detected
    y: max_score
    label: precursor_id
    color: star_support
    size: total_reads

- component: card
  title: Novel precursors
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of novel precursors and the ring splits them by whether star-arm reads support them. It answers how many candidates carry the Dicer signature.
    How to read: a large share without star support means many candidates rest on mature-arm reads alone and need validation, for instance in more samples.
  column: star_support
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: star_support
  caption: precursors, by star-arm support
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Samples per precursor
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of samples that report a precursor and the box shows the spread. It answers how reproducible the candidates are.
    How to read: miRDeep2 flags candidates found in multiple independent samples as high confidence, so a box near 1 means most calls are one-off.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21911355/
  column: samples_detected
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: samples, quartiles over precursors

- component: card
  title: Best score per precursor
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median of the best miRDeep2 score of each precursor and the box shows the spread. It answers how confident the discovery is overall.
    How to read: higher scores are more probable genuine miRNAs. Scores can be negative, so compare the box with the score-cutoff survey tile rather than with zero.
  column: max_score
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: score, quartiles over precursors

- component: interactive
  title: Samples per precursor
  description: Restricts the tiles to precursors reported by a chosen range of samples. Raise the lower
    bound to keep only reproducible candidates.
  interactive_type: RangeSlider
  column_name: samples_detected

- component: table
  title: Novel precursor table
  description: |-
    Each row is a novel precursor merged across samples, with its locus, best score, reads per arm, randfold share and the mature, star and precursor sequences. It answers which candidates to validate and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by score or samples detected, and check the randfold share and any Rfam hit, since a hit to a known non-miRNA family argues against a call.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: precursor_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: prediction_scores
  title: Prediction score against read support
  description: |-
    Each point is a precursor in one sample: its total reads on a log axis and its miRDeep2 score, coloured by novel or known (already in miRBase). It answers how novel candidates compare with the known miRNAs the run re-detected.
    How to read: known miRNAs show what a confident call looks like for this dataset. Novel candidates scoring like them are credible; low-scoring ones on few reads are likely noise. Open the table to read the sequences.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median miRDeep2 score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of miRDeep2. The README sets a score cut-off of 0 only for which novel candidates its overview table lists, and surveys cut-offs from -10 to 10.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rajewsky-lab/mirdeep2/master/README.md
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    x_title: Total reads on the precursor
    y_title: miRDeep2 score
    log_x: true
    legend_pos: bottom
    top_n_labels: 6
  roles:
    x: total_reads
    y: score
    label: prediction_id
    color: category

- component: card
  title: Scored precursors
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of precursors miRDeep2 scored and the ring splits them into novel candidates and known miRBase precursors. It answers how much of the output is discovery.
    How to read: a known share that is very low means the library missed most expected miRNAs, which argues for checking the library quality first.
  column: category
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - mode
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: category
  caption: precursors, novel and known
  headline: true

- component: card
  title: Score of predictions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median miRDeep2 score and the box shows the spread. It answers how strongly the predictions are supported overall.
    How to read: filter to novel or known with the category selector and compare the two boxes. A novel box far below the known one means weak candidates.
  column: score
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: score, quartiles over predictions

- component: interactive
  title: Prediction category
  description: Filters the tiles to novel candidates, known miRBase precursors or both.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: category

- component: table
  title: Prediction table
  description: |-
    Each row is a precursor in one sample with its score, true-positive estimate, read counts per arm, randfold result and locus. It answers which predictions to follow up and lets a row selection filter the rest of the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by score and check the true-positive estimate and its standard deviation together, as a wide deviation means an uncertain estimate.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: prediction_id

- component: advanced_viz
  id: signal_to_noise_curve
  title: Signal-to-noise by score cut-off
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the signal-to-noise ratio of novel predictions, against permuted structures, at each integer score cut-off. It answers how stringent the score cut-off must be before predictions rise above the noise.
    How to read: pick a cut-off where the curve has risen and flattened, and read the recovery curve beside it to see what that costs in known miRNAs. A flat curve near 1 means the data hold little signal over noise.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. The survey covers cut-offs from -10 to 10, and miRDeep2's README sets a default of 0 only for which novel candidates its overview table lists.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rajewsky-lab/mirdeep2/master/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: miRDeep2 score cut-off
    y_title: Signal-to-noise ratio
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: score_cutoff
    y: signal_to_noise

- component: advanced_viz
  id: known_recovery_curve
  title: Known miRNAs recovered by score cut-off
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample: the share of known miRBase miRNAs present in the data that miRDeep2 recovers at each integer score cut-off. It answers what a stricter cut-off costs in sensitivity.
    How to read: a curve that stays high up to the cut-off you choose means the stricter filter loses few known miRNAs. A steep fall marks the cut-off beyond which real miRNAs are discarded.
    Lines and annotations: none are drawn. miRDeep2's README sets a score cut-off of 0 only for which novel candidates its overview table lists.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rajewsky-lab/mirdeep2/master/README.md
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: miRDeep2 score cut-off
    y_title: Known miRNAs detected (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: sample
    x: score_cutoff
    y: known_detected_pct

- component: figure
  title: Novel precursors by score cut-off
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample: the number of novel precursors reported at each score cut-off. It answers how many candidates survive as the filter tightens.
    How to read: a steep early drop means most candidates have low scores. Combine it with the signal-to-noise curve to choose a cut-off that keeps a manageable list.
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: score_cutoff
    y: novel_reported
    color: sample
    labels:
      score_cutoff: miRDeep2 score cut-off
      novel_reported: Novel precursors reported
      sample: Sample

- component: table
  title: Score cut-off survey table
  description: |-
    Each row is a sample and an integer score cut-off with the novel predictions, estimated false and true positives, known miRNAs recovered and the signal-to-noise ratio. It answers the exact numbers behind the curves.
    How to read: sort by sample and cut-off to follow one curve, or by signal-to-noise to find the cut-off that maximises it.
